headline: NEW HIGH-GRADE SILVER VEIN at Idaho's Historic Bunker Hill Mine Ahead of June Restart — 11.3 oz/ton AgEq
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR) expanded its newly discovered Cate-8 silver-lead vein in Idaho's historic Bunker Hill mine, with the best drill hole returning 15.5 ft at 11.34 oz/ton AgEq. Management expects the zone to improve 2027–2028 silver output as the 1,800 tpd operation moves toward its scheduled June 2026 restart; an investor webinar was held June 3 to discuss results.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,500 as JOLTS Data Beats Hard — Friday Payrolls Now the Line in the Sand for Fed Hike Bets
snippet: Gold held above $4,500 per ounce on June 3 after Tuesday's JOLTS report showed US job openings surging to a near two-year high, raising the odds of a year-end Fed rate hike to 40%. Markets now wait on Friday's nonfarm payrolls print as the next major catalyst; oil's pullback has helped temper inflation fears and given metals room to consolidate.

headline: CHINA'S METAL, AMERICA'S CLOCK: Nevada Tungsten Mine Makes Its Move as 2027 Defense Procurement Ban Looms
snippet: A Nevada tungsten project advanced its exploration plans as U.S. defense supply chains face a January 1, 2027 deadline barring procurement of Chinese, Russian, Iranian, and North Korean tungsten. China controls roughly 80% of global supply of the dense metal used in armor-piercing ammunition, cutting tools, and semiconductor manufacturing.

headline: UTAH URANIUM PROJECT TAKES SHAPE: Anfield Energy Completes Phase One Construction at Velvet-Wood
snippet: Anfield Energy Inc. completed phase one surface construction at its Velvet-Wood uranium and vanadium project in Utah and is now advancing to phase two mine construction. The project is one of a growing number of U.S. uranium-vanadium assets moving toward production amid sustained spot prices above $80/lb and bipartisan support for domestic nuclear fuel supply.

headline: WORKER KILLED at Endeavour Mining's Lafigué Gold Mine in Côte d'Ivoire; Operations Suspended
snippet: Endeavour Mining reported a fatal accident at its Lafigué gold mine in Côte d'Ivoire — a flagship growth asset that produced over 315,000 ounces in 2025 — with operations suspended pending investigation. The incident is a reminder of the operational and jurisdictional risks embedded in West African production, often underweighted by retail investors drawn to the low-cost profiles of African gold miners.

headline: URANIUM SPOT SLIPS BELOW $85 — Near-Term Pressure, But Utility Under-Contracting Keeps the Long Trade Alive
snippet: Uranium spot eased below $85 per pound in late May — its lowest in two months — after peaking at $101.41 in Q1 2026 as geopolitical volatility reduced risk appetite. Analysts note that prolonged utility under-contracting and limited new mine pipelines maintain the structural supply gap, with Denison's Phoenix ISR mine now under construction in Saskatchewan and Urenco USA planning a 50% enrichment capacity expansion.

headline: JUNE 30 TARIFF DECISION LOOMS: Copper Faces U.S. Policy Roulette — 15% Import Duty Could Hit in 2027
snippet: The U.S. Commerce Secretary faces a June 30 deadline to recommend whether to impose phased import duties on refined copper — 15% starting January 2027 rising to 30% by 2028 — as part of a Section 232 review. Copper producers say domestic US mine output covers only 1.1 million of the 1.6 million tonnes the country consumes annually, meaning tariffs could amplify price pressures without resolving supply dependency.

headline: MONUMENT MINING Posts $22.65M Net Profit in Q3 Fiscal 2026 as Selinsing Gold Plant Runs Near Capacity
snippet: Monument Mining (TSX: MMY) reported a net profit of $22.65 million ($0.07/share) in Q3 fiscal 2026 as strong gold prices boosted margins at its Selinsing Gold Mine in Malaysia. The company also recently released drill results highlighting expansion potential at the project's periphery, reflecting the broader theme of mid-tier producers using elevated prices to fund reserve growth.

headline: $2.2 BILLION GUYANA GOLD MERGER: G2 Goldfields Shareholders Vote June 16 on G Mining Ventures Takeover
snippet: G2 Goldfields shareholders vote on June 16 on G Mining Ventures' $2.2 billion all-share acquisition, consolidating two adjacent Guyana gold projects — Oko-Ghanie and Oko West — into a combined operation targeting 500,000+ ounces annually at some of the lowest costs in the Americas. The deal includes a G3 Goldfields spin-out unlocking over C$1 billion in projected synergies.
